issue_title: Solar position values are incorrect when using DatetimeIndex with unit='us'
issue_body:
**Describe the bug**
Solar elevation values are wrong when using the default `nrel_numpy` method

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```
import pvlib

# Example usage:
latitude = 37.7749  # Replace with the desired latitude
longitude = -122.4194  # Replace with the desired longitude

# Create a sample DatetimeIndex (replace with your own datetime index)
date_index = pd.date_range(start='2023-01-01', end='2023-01-05', freq='H')

correct_results = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(
    time=date_index,
    latitude=37.804363,
    longitude=-122.271111,
    method="pyephem"
)

incorrect_results = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(
    time=date_index,
    latitude=37.804363,
    longitude=-122.271111,
) 
```

**Expected behavior**
solar altitude should be on a negative/positive cycle throughout a day

**Screenshots**

**Versions:**
 - ``pvlib.__version__``: 0.10.2
 - ``pandas.__version__``: 2.1.4
 - python: 3.10.13

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.


There's obviously a workaround, but this was a surprising error, is this known?

hints_text: I get the same results in both cases. If the elevation isn't lined up with time, then the datetimes need to be localized with the correct timezone. Interesting, FWIW this is what the code looks like which generated the error on my end, and you can see the elevation data is off (no negatives throughout a day). Not sure it's worth figuring out reconstructing this exact index, but in case you see why this index might be different: I think the problem is that the time index in that screenshot has dtype `datetime64[us, US/Pacific]`, but `spa_python` is assuming the input is represented in nanoseconds: https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/blob/8057393e6eaa57ca1ea60bc79205b94d00b33e42/pvlib/solarposition.py#L369 Here is code to recreate the issue from scratch: ```python import pandas as pd import pvlib for unit in ['ns', 'us']: index = pd.date_range('2023-12-09', freq='H', periods=6, tz='US/Pacific', unit=unit) sp = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(time=index, latitude=37.804363, longitude=-122.271111) print(f'Results for {unit=}:') print(sp['elevation']) ``` ``` Results for unit='ns': 2023-12-09 00:00:00-08:00 -74.994002 2023-12-09 01:00:00-08:00 -70.408287 2023-12-09 02:00:00-08:00 -60.497812 2023-12-09 03:00:00-08:00 -49.067690 2023-12-09 04:00:00-08:00 -37.255747 2023-12-09 05:00:00-08:00 -25.482336 Freq: H, Name: elevation, dtype: float64 Results for unit='us': 2023-12-09 00:00:00-08:00 13.682861 2023-12-09 01:00:00-08:00 13.692004 2023-12-09 02:00:00-08:00 13.701146 2023-12-09 03:00:00-08:00 13.710287 2023-12-09 04:00:00-08:00 13.719425 2023-12-09 05:00:00-08:00 13.728563 Freq: H, Name: elevation, dtype: float64 ``` @patricksheehan, just to be sure, when you run the original reproducer code in https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/issues/1932#issue-2049609747, do you observe the issue? Or is it only with that `us` index in the notebook? @kandersolar `unit` was introduced at pandas 2.0.0, I checked this with 1.5.3, maybe that's why I didn't reproduce the error. Well, I think `ns` is still the default unit in pandas 2.x. The only way I know how to get an index with `us` units is to explicitly request it (either specifying `unit='us'` when creating the index or converting an existing index with `.astype('datetime64[us]')`). I'm curious how the index in @patricksheehan's example came to have `us` units :) `1e9` and `10**9` show up in several places in `solarposition.py`, so we might need to fix this problem in a few different places. @kandersolar thanks for looking at that, you're totally right that the `us` units is the culprit, the OG code I posted works for me as well (apologies for the bad test code, I always settle at 50% effort for reporting weird things vs not reporting at all). I'm also honestly not sure how the `us` unit got in there, this is from a client's pickled `DataFrame` so who knows ;). It's a good heads up for an issue that needs fixed, I don't think we want to limit pvlib to pandas < 2.0.0 Another instance of this bug in the wild (pandas 2.0.2): https://groups.google.com/g/pvlib-python/c/xDcgxTwmGTA I'd like to do my bit with this issue since I've also experienced this looking to optimize memory usage using rougher precision with `datetime[s]`. Indeed, [on the Internet](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15203623/convert-pandas-datetimeindex-to-unix-time) the `// 10**9` solution is clearly favoured, and it really makes sense, since current `pandas.DatetimeIndex` docs state the following as kandersolar noted before. ``` dtype : numpy.dtype or DatetimeTZDtype or str, default None Note that the only NumPy dtype allowed is datetime64[ns]. ``` 1. This would be a reason to consider this a not-PVLIB issue. I'm not really in favour of that. 1. A possible solution that **I haven't tried yet** could be: 1. Converting to `datetime.datetime` with [pd.DatetimeIndex.to_pydatetime](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DatetimeIndex.to_pydatetime.html#pandas.DatetimeIndex.to_pydatetime). It is not affected by the underlying `dtype`. 1. Follow [this StackOverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/19801727/convert-datetime-to-unix-timestamp-and-convert-it-back-in-python). Or [this one](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8777753/converting-datetime-date-to-utc-timestamp-in-python), mentioned in the former. 1. Another possibility is to warn about the underlying type of `pd.DatetimeIndex` in the [.get_solarposition](https://pvlib-python.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/generated/pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition.html) docs. 1. Regarding doing the conversion manually in PVLIB, it is feasible. I've checked Pandas is capable of doing the right introspection of the `dtype` for non-`ns` data types: ```python >>> import pandas as pd >>> from importlib.metadata import version >>> pd.DatetimeIndex(['2023-09-06']).dtype dtype('>> pd.DatetimeIndex(['2023-09-06'], dtype='datetime64[ns]').dtype dtype('>> pd.DatetimeIndex(['2023-09-06'], dtype='datetime64[s]').dtype dtype('>> pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.date_range('2023-09-03', '2023-09-06', unit='s')).dtype dtype('>> pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.date_range('2023-09-03', '2023-09-06', unit='s')).to_pydatetime() array([datetime.datetime(2023, 9, 3, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2023, 9, 4, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2023, 9, 5, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2023, 9, 6, 0, 0)], dtype=object) >>> version("pandas") '2.0.2' ``` I advocate for doing no. 2. `.to_pydatetime` exists since Pandas 1.0.0 I may work on this on the future, but if someone else wants, I encourage doing so. Thanks @echedey-ls! I think we really need to have pvlib work with `us` and other units. The pandas [docs](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/timeseries.html#from-timestamps-to-epoch) suggest this method of calculating unix time, which seems to be working well in my tests: ```python (stamps - pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01")) // pd.Timedelta("1s") ``` I have a PR in the works with this approach. The main thing is coming up with comprehensive tests... Oh, wow, I didn't find that earlier! That's incredibly Pythonic. Good luck with the tests, that's the worst part.
